messages:
Sara L: Heads-up — deployed audit-schema v2 to canary tenant acme-45 about 10m ago. We're seeing the audit-processor queue grow and a lot of 429s from KMS. Kicking this to eng-security/ops: any quick ideas?

Josh M: ugh. do we know if KMS is being called per-event or per-batch?

Sara L: per-event today. v2 added `customer_key_id` field and we call KMS.Encrypt on the event payload before handing to the indexer.

Dilip: yep that's the issue. at 1k rps that becomes 1k kms calls/s. KMS has soft limits and we hit throttles. Logs show repeated 429 + exponential backoff.

Maria SRE: queue depth at audit-processor: 118k. CPU on the shipper pods at 95%. ES indexing latency up, cost estimates show ~3x IO because of larger encrypted blob sizes.

Sara L: this is the canary, so good we caught it early. thoughts on mitigations: batch KMS envelopes, sign locally, or fall back to unencrypted payload + audit event marker? need risk tradeoffs.

Andi: for short-term canary rollback is fastest. we can revert to schema v1 for that tenant and stop the KMS calls. ops-oncall can do a rollback toggle?

ops-oncall: I can flip the feature flag for acme-45 now. prepping a rollback in 30m. any non-blockers to do that?

Josh M: long-term: switch to envelope encryption. flow: generate a per-batch DEK, call KMS once to wrap the DEK, then encrypt many events using DEK locally. saves N->1 KMS calls.

Dilip: agreed. sketch: 
```
for batch in batches(events):
  dek = random_bytes(32)
  wrapped = kms.wrapKey(dek, customer_key_id)
  for ev in batch:
    ev.payload = aes_gcm_encrypt(ev.payload, dek)
  send({wrapped_dek: wrapped, events: batch})
```
This reduces KMS calls to ~batch_count. Need to pick batch size carefully to meet latency SLOs.

Maria SRE: batching helps but increases memory pressure and slightly higher tail latency. for indexing cost: compressed encrypted blobs are less compressible, so we'll see ES storage and IO increase. we should run a cost sim: +storage, +IO, +kms. Preliminary estimate for full rollout at current traffic: +$1.2k/day in storage+IO and +$800/day in KMS.

Sara L: ouch. can we mitigate storage by storing only an envelope reference in ES and moving payloads to a blob store (S3) with lifecycle? index small metadata for searchability and link to S3.

Dilip: that shifts cost from ES to S3 (cheaper) and reduces indexing load. but it complicates customer-facing audit validation (customers expect full event payload in the audit API).

Andi: maybe keep two-tier: searchable index with minimal fields (actor, action, resource, timestamp, S3 pointer) + batched payloads in S3 encrypted. customer-facing event validation can rehydrate from S3 when needed. we may need to update contracts/SLAs.

security-bot: NOTE: any change to how we store customer audit data needs a privacy review and update to the security design doc per compliance checklist.

Sara L: good call. we'll open a PR for design review. action items for now: 1) ops-oncall to toggle rollback for acme-45 in 30m; 2) Dilip + Josh to prototype envelope batching with batch size 50 and measure tail latency; 3) Maria to run cost sim for ES vs S3 storage with current event size distribution; 4) Sara to kick off privacy/compliance review.

Josh M: quick note — also consider per-tenant KMS quotas + circuit breaker so a single noisy tenant doesn't blow up whole fleet. per-tenant token bucket and early reject + sampling could buy time.

Maria SRE: +1 to per-tenant QoS. we already have tenant tagging in the pipeline, adding token-bucket is low-risk.

Dilip: for prototyping, I'll stub KMS with a local kms-mock that returns 200 for wrapKey and measure. will post benchmark later.

Sara L: thanks all. I'll post an updated timeline after rollback. :eyes:
